note: What IngredientParser should make of real ingredient lines. Sources: the examples in spec sections 1a, 5.6a and 5.7, the shapes NYT Cooking and Mealime actually produce, and the kinds of line someone types into the manual entry form. tools/resource-lint checks each case is self-consistent: the unit exists, the quantity is sane, and every piece of expected output actually appears in the input, so no case can expect something that was never there.

confidenceMeaning.high: Save it without asking. Section 1a: confirm only the lines we are unsure about.
confidenceMeaning.medium: Usable, but show it on the review screen.
confidenceMeaning.low: We got something out of it, but a person should look.

cases.name: large lemon
cases.why: section 5.6a's example of a well formed NYT line. Size words stay in the name, which section 4 says is kept as written; resolving them is CanonicalMatcher's job.

cases.name: sesame oil
cases.why: the line section 1a says Mealime failed to merge with the one below

cases.name: soy sauce
cases.why: unicode fractions arrive from pasted web text

cases.input: 1 bunch (about 1 pound) asparagus, tough ends removed and stalks cut into 1/2-inch pieces
cases.name: asparagus
cases.preparation: tough ends removed and stalks cut into 1/2-inch pieces
cases.why: section 1a's example of exactly what Mealime kept as a raw string and never merged

cases.input: 4 scallions, white and green parts separated, thinly sliced
cases.name: scallions
cases.preparation: white and green parts separated, thinly sliced
cases.why: everything after the first comma is preparation, commas and all

cases.name: parsley
cases.why: preparation before the name instead of after a comma. Common, and less certain than the comma form.

cases.name: chickpeas
cases.why: section 5.7: the shape Mealime stores as a free text quantity

cases.name: black beans
cases.why: the can size runs into the quantity with no parentheses to separate it

cases.input: 1 (13.5 oz) can coconut milk, full fat
cases.name: coconut milk
garlic
cases.why: a range takes the lower bound: buying too little is recoverable at the stove, buying too much is waste

cases.name: potatoes
cases.why: an en dash, which is what a copy and paste from the web gives

cases.name: head garlic
cases.why: head is not one of the sixteen units in section 4, so it stays in the name rather than being invented as a unit

cases.input: Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
cases.name: Kosher salt and black pepper
cases.why: two items on one line. We keep it whole and flag it rather than guessing at a split.

cases.name: Juice of 1 lemon
cases.why: the number belongs to the lemon, not to the juice, so a leading-number rule would read it wrong

cases.name: plus 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
cases.why: a compound quantity. Parsed badly on purpose, and flagged, rather than silently dropping the extra.

cases.name: Butter
cases.why: units match case insensitively, the name keeps its case
